title: Static and Media Files in Production
description: Serve static assets and user‑uploaded media correctly in production.

slides.title: The collectstatic Command 📦
slides.content:
In production, Django does not serve static files (CSS, JS, images). You must collect them into a single directory and configure your web server to serve them.

```bash
python manage.py collectstatic
```

This copies all static files from each app’s `static/` folder and any `STATICFILES_DIRS` into `STATIC_ROOT`.

Set `STATIC_ROOT` to a directory outside your project, e.g., `/var/www/static/`.

slides.title: Serving Static Files with Whitenoise
slides.content:
A simple way to serve static files in production without configuring a separate server is to use **Whitenoise**.

```bash
pip install whitenoise
```

Add to `MIDDLEWARE` (after SecurityMiddleware):
```python
MIDDLEWARE = [
    'django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware',
    'whitenoise.middleware.WhiteNoiseMiddleware',
    ...
]
```

Then set `STATIC_ROOT` and run `collectstatic`. Whitenoise will serve static files efficiently.

quizData.question: What is the purpose of `collectstatic`?
options: To gather all static files into a single directory for production
To serve static files during development
quizData.explanation: `collectstatic` copies static files to `STATIC_ROOT` so they can be served by a web server or Whitenoise.

slides.title: Media Files (User Uploads) 📸
slides.content:
User‑uploaded files (profile pictures, post images) should not be served by Django either. Use:
- **Amazon S3** or other cloud storage for scalability.
- **Web server** (Nginx, Apache) to serve from `MEDIA_ROOT`.

For local testing in production, you can use Whitenoise for media as well, but it’s not recommended for many files.

Always set `MEDIA_URL` and ensure your web server is configured to serve files from `MEDIA_ROOT`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use a CDN for static files

For better performance, serve static files from a CDN (e.g., CloudFront, Cloudflare) after collecting them to a cloud storage bucket (S3).
